'''Laszlo Lorand''' (23 March 1923 – 6 December 2018) was a [[Hungarian-American]] biochemist who studied clotting of blood and other bodily fluids. A professor emeritus in [[molecular biology|cell and molecular biology]] at the [[Feinberg School of Medicine]], Lorand was a longtime professor in the departments of chemistry and molecular biosciences at [[Northwestern University]] before transferring to Northwestern's medical school. Lorand was a co-discoverer of the substance that later became known as [[factor XIII]]. He was a member of the [[National Academy of Sciences]].

==Biography==
Lorand was born in [[Győr|Győr, Hungary]]. His father was murdered in [[Auschwitz]], but he himself managed to avoid being sent there.<ref>{{cite news|url=https://magazine.alumni.leeds.ac.uk/cold-war-biochemist/ |title=The biochemist who came in from the cold|date=February 2021 |publisher=Leeds University Alumni Magazine
|access-date=2021-03-03}}</ref> Lorand was a Holocaust survivor and [[History of the Jews in Hungary|Jewish]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.legacy.com/us/obituaries/chicagotribune/name/laszlo-lorand-obituary?pid=191007986 |title=Laszlo Lorand|website=[[Legacy.com]]|access-date=3 March 2021}}</ref> He submitted a record of his experiences in the Holocaust to the Yad Vaashem witness data base programme in Israel.<ref>{{cite web | url=https://www.mbl.edu/obituaries/laszlo-lorand/ | title=Laszlo Lorand }}</ref>

He studied medicine in Hungary and received an [[absolutorium]] from the [[Eötvös Loránd University|University of Budapest]].<ref name="Symposium">{{cite web|title=Lorand honored at biomedical symposium|date=25 November 2013 |url=http://news.feinberg.northwestern.edu/2013/11/lorand_symposium/|publisher=[[Feinberg School of Medicine]]|access-date=November 15, 2015}}</ref> In Hungary, he was mentored by biochemists [[Albert Szent-Györgyi]] and [[Kalman Laki]]. Owing to events related to the [[Cold War]], Lorand left Budapest for England in December 1948, just after finishing his medical school coursework.<ref name=JTH>{{cite journal|last1=Lorand|first1=L|title=Factor XIII and the clotting of fibrinogen: From basic research to medicine|journal=[[Journal of Thrombosis and Haemostasis]]|date=July 2005|volume=3|issue=7|pages=1337–1348|doi=10.1111/j.1538-7836.2005.01213.x|pmid=15978088|s2cid=46470020|doi-access=free}}</ref> The biomolecular structure department at the [[University of Leeds]] was chaired by physicist and molecular biologist [[William Astbury]]. He became interested in Lorand's prior work on the viscosity of [[fibrin]].<ref name=JTH/> Lorand earned a Ph.D. in biomolecular structure from Leeds in 1951.<ref name=Feinberg>{{cite web|title=Laszlo Lorand, PhD|url=http://www.feinberg.northwestern.edu/faculty-profiles/az/profile.html?xid=15545|publisher=[[Feinberg School of Medicine]]|access-date=November 15, 2015}}</ref>

Lorand was a professor at [[Wayne State University]], and then he came to Northwestern and spent many years in the departments of chemistry and molecular biosciences. In 1993, he transferred to Northwestern's [[Feinberg School of Medicine]].<ref name=Symposium/> Lorand is associated with the Feinberg Cardiovascular Research Institute.<ref name=FCVRI>{{cite web|title=A-Z Faculty|url=http://www.fcvri.northwestern.edu/faculty/index.html|publisher=[[Feinberg School of Medicine]]|access-date=November 15, 2015}}</ref> He was the co-editor of ''Proteolytic Enzymes'', a volume of the scientific series ''[[Methods in Enzymology]]''.<ref name=Proteolytic>{{cite book|title=Proteolytic enzymes|publisher=[[WorldCat]]|oclc=155908}}</ref> He was a co-discoverer of [[factor XIII]], which was formerly referred to as Laki–Lorand factor and fibrin stabilizing factor.<ref name=BBRC>{{cite journal|last1=Chandrasekhar|first1=N|last2=Osbahr|first2=A|last3=Laki|first3=K|title=The mode of action of the Laki-Lorand factor in the clotting of fibrinogen|journal=[[Biochemical and Biophysical Research Communications]]|date=March 9, 1964|volume=15|issue=2|pages=182–187|doi=10.1016/0006-291X(64)90321-3|pmid=26410914}}</ref>

In 1983, Lorand was awarded an honorary [[Doctor of Science]] from the [[University of Illinois at Chicago]].<ref name=Trustees>{{cite web|title=Board of Trustees Minutes – 1984|url=http://uihistories.library.illinois.edu/cgi-bin/rview_browsepdf?REPOSID=8&ID=8115&pagenum=183|publisher=[[University of Illinois system|University of Illinois]]|access-date=November 16, 2015}}</ref> He was elected to the [[National Academy of Sciences]] in 1987.<ref name=NASLorand>{{cite web|title=Laszlo Lorand|url=https://www.nasonline.org/directory-entry/laszlo-lorand-ynk24m/|publisher=[[National Academy of Sciences]]|access-date=November 15, 2015}}</ref>

Lorand met Joyce Bruner, also a scientist, in 1953. They later married, and Joyce Bruner-Lorand collaborated with her husband on NIH-funded studies at Northwestern for many years. Joyce died in 2010.<ref name=Joyce>{{cite web|title=Joyce Bruner-Lorand|url=http://www.mbl.edu/obituaries/joyce-bruner-lorand/|publisher=[[Marine Biological Laboratory]]|access-date=November 15, 2015}}</ref>

Lorand died in 2018.<ref name="Obit">{{cite web |title=Laszlo Lorand |url=https://www.mbl.edu/obituaries/laszlo-lorand/ |website=www.mbl.edu |access-date=May 17, 2020}}</ref>
